body.title: Article body
body.intro: Long-form type: paragraphs with a loose line, headings with a hairline above, numbered lists, and a quote with a heavy rule at its start. The share column sits beside it.
body.note: The editor doesn't make images or tables inside the text today; a photo with its caption uses the "Image with caption" part.
body.heading: Why governance manuals fail in their first week
body.p1: Most manuals I've seen didn't fail because they were badly written. They failed because whoever wrote them never asked the people who would use them: what do you do when a decision lands on you and you don't know who owns it?
body.h2: Three reasons that keep coming back
body.li1: The manual describes the institution as it should be, not as it is.
body.li2: No one owns updating it once it's approved.
body.li3: New staff don't know it exists.
body.quote: A rule that staff can't explain to a colleague is a rule they won't follow.
body.p2: If you're working on a manual now, start from the question, not the template.

items.q: Is a consultation paid through the website?
items.a: No. The website is for getting in touch. We agree everything in writing in the conversation before any commitment.

items.q: Can our organization's name stay confidential?
items.a: Yes. The project shows a general label for the organization, and its name appears nowhere on the site.

items.q: Do you work outside the Arab region?
